lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are designing an Azure order-processing system that will contain the Azure resources shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783707864292-x5ydxlmp.png)  
  
The order-processing system will use the following transaction flow:  
  
- A customer will place an order by using App1.  
- When the order is received, App1 will generate a message to check product availability at vendor 1 and vendor 2.  
- An integration component will process the message and then trigger either Function1 or Function2, depending on the order type.  
- When a vendor confirms product availability, Function1 or Function2 will generate a status message for App1.  
- All transaction steps will be logged to storage1.

Azure Service Bus, Event Grid, and Event Hubs Capture are all messaging or ingestion mechanisms, but none of them natively performs the type-based branching and multi-step orchestration that an integration component doing this routing and invocation logic needs.

**Learn more:** [Pipelines and activities in Azure Data Factory](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/data-factory/concepts-pipelines-activities) · [Azure Function activity in Azure Data Factory](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/data-factory/control-flow-azure-function-activity)

Solution: You use Azure Front Door to enable access to the app.  
  
Does this achieve the goal?
questions.explanation:
Azure Front Door provides global load balancing across healthy origins and can route traffic to an alternative origin when one becomes unavailable, supporting regional-outage resiliency. Azure Front Door WAF also supports rate-limit rules to limit requests from clients.\
\
**Learn more:** [Accelerate and Secure Your Web Application with Azure Front Door](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/frontdoor/scenarios) · [WAF Rate Limiting for Azure Front Door](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/web-application-firewall/afds/waf-front-door-rate-limit)

questions.question:
Solution: You use Azure Traffic Manager to provide access to the app.  
  
Does this achieve the goal?
questions.explanation:
Azure Traffic Manager can distribute traffic across endpoints and route users to healthy endpoints when a regional endpoint becomes unavailable, but it does not enforce request rate limits. Therefore, it cannot satisfy the required rate-limiting, load-balancing, and regional-outage requirements as a complete solution.\
\
**Learn more:** [Traffic Manager routing methods](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/traffic-manager/traffic-manager-routing-methods) · [Control Azure App Service traffic with Azure Traffic Manager](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/app-service/web-sites-traffic-manager)

questions.question:
Solution: Use Azure Load Balancer to provide access to the app.  
  
Does this satisfy the goal?
questions.explanation:
Azure Load Balancer operates at Layer 4 for TCP and UDP traffic and does not provide application-layer rate limiting. A Global Load Balancer can balance traffic across regions and support regional failover, but it cannot by itself satisfy the required rate-limiting capability.\
\
**Learn more:** [Troubleshoot Azure Load Balancer limitations](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/troubleshoot/azure/load-balancer/troubleshoot-load-balancer-platform-limitations) · [Global load balancer - Azure Load Balancer](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/load-balancer/cross-region-overview)

questions.question:

questions.explanation:
Azure Application Gateway v2 is a single-region service, so it becomes unavailable if its region has an outage. Multi-region resiliency requires separate regional gateways and a global load-balancing service to route and fail over traffic between them. Application Gateway WAF v2 can support rate limiting, but that does not satisfy the regional-outage requirement by itself.\
\
**Learn more:** [Reliability in Azure Application Gateway v2](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/reliability/reliability-application-gateway-v2) · [Create rate limiting custom rules for Application Gateway WAF v2](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/web-application-firewall/ag/rate-limiting-configure)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an app called App1 that uses an Azure Blob Storage container named app1data.  
  
App1 uploads a cumulative transaction-log file named File1.txt to a block blob in app1data every hour. File1.txt contains transaction data only for the current day.  
  
You must ensure that the final uploaded version of File1.txt from any day can be restored for up to 30 days after it is overwritten. The solution must use the least possible storage space.  
  
What should the solution include?
questions.explanation:
A blob snapshot can be taken once per day to preserve that day’s final state and retained for 30 days. Snapshots are billed for unique blocks, so they provide the required daily recovery points without retaining every hourly overwrite. Blob soft delete and blob versioning automatically retain data for each overwrite, creating unnecessary hourly recovery states and using more storage.

**Learn more:** [Blob snapshots - Azure Storage](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/blobs/snapshots-overview) · [Choosing between blob soft delete and blob versioning](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/blobs/soft-delete-vs-versioning-options)

You need to recommend a solution that lets the cloud services communicate transaction information asynchronously by using XML messages.  
  
What should you include in the recommendation?
questions.explanation:
Azure Queue Storage provides message queues that decouple distributed application components, allowing one service to place transaction messages in a queue for another service to process asynchronously. Queue messages must be compatible with UTF-8 XML requests; XML markup carried as message content must be Base64-encoded.

**Learn more:** [Introduction to Azure Queue Storage](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/queues/storage-queues-introduction) · [Put Message (Azure Queue Storage REST API)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/rest/api/storageservices/put-message)

You need to recommend a solution for generating a monthly report of all new Azure Resource Manager (ARM) resource deployments in your Azure subscription.  
  
What should the recommendation include?
questions.explanation:

The Business Critical service tier maintains multiple synchronous database replicas and supports zone redundancy, which distributes replicas across availability zones. You are planning a storage solution. The solution must satisfy these requirements:  
  
- Support at least 500 requests per second.  
- Support large image, video, and audio streams.  
  
Which type of Azure Storage account should you provision?
questions.explanation:
A standard general-purpose v2 account supports Azure Blob Storage, which is designed for streaming video and audio. Its block blobs support objects up to approximately 190.7 TiB and have a target rate of up to 3,000 requests per second per blob, satisfying both the large-stream and 500-requests-per-second requirements. Premium block blob accounts are primarily recommended when high transaction rates, smaller objects, or consistently low latency specifically require premium performance.

**Learn more:** [Introduction to Azure Blob Storage](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/blobs/storage-blobs-introduction) · [Scalability and performance targets for Blob storage](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/blobs/scalability-targets)

You are developing a sales application that will include several Azure cloud services and process different parts of a transaction. Different cloud services will handle customer orders, billing, payment, inventory, and shipping.  
  
You need to recommend a solution that enables the cloud services to communicate transaction information asynchronously by using XML messages.  
  
What should you include in the recommendation?
questions.explanation:
Azure Service Bus provides durable queues and publish-subscribe topics for reliable asynchronous communication between decoupled services. Its message payloads can contain structured data such as XML, making it suitable for exchanging transaction information among order, billing, payment, inventory, and shipping services.

**Learn more:** [What is Azure Service Bus?](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/service-bus-messaging/service-bus-messaging-overview) · [Asynchronous messaging patterns and high availability](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/service-bus-messaging/service-bus-async-messaging)

You need to recommend a service for storing and querying the data.  
  
Which two services can you recommend? Each correct answer presents a complete solution.  
  
**NOTE:** Each correct selection is worth one point.
questions.explanation: For 50,000 IoT devices streaming 50,000 records per second with near-real-time visualization, two services meet all requirements: Azure Cosmos DB SQL API provides horizontally scalable storage and SQL-based querying for high-volume telemetry, while Azure Time Series Insights was purpose-built to ingest, store, query, and visualize time-series IoT data in near real-time. Azure Table Storage (A) cannot handle the throughput, and Azure Event Grid (B) is only a broker without storage or query capabilities.

- Allow virtual machines to be created only in specified regions.  
- Allow only specified virtual machine sizes to be created.  
  
What should you include in the recommendation?
questions.explanation:
Azure Policy provides deny-based governance controls for resource deployments. The built-in Allowed locations policy restricts deployment to specified regions, and the Allowed virtual machine size SKUs policy restricts the VM SKUs that can be deployed.

**Learn more:** [Azure Policy overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/governance/policy/overview) · [Built-in policy definitions for Azure Virtual Machines](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-machines/policy-reference)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company hosts 300 virtual machines in a VMware environment. The virtual machines differ in size and have varying utilization levels.  
  
You plan to migrate all the virtual machines to Azure.  
  
You need to recommend the number and sizes of Azure virtual machines required to migrate the existing workloads to Azure. The solution must minimize administrative effort.  
  
What should you use to make the recommendation?
questions.explanation:
Azure Migrate Discovery and Assessment evaluates VMware workloads and can use collected CPU, memory, disk, and network performance data to produce right-sized Azure VM recommendations. This supports sizing the migrated estate according to actual utilization while minimizing manual assessment work.

**Learn more:** [Overview of Azure Migrate assessment types](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/migrate/concepts-assessment-overview?view=migrate) · [Performance vs. as-is on-premises assessments](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/migrate/target-right-sizing?view=migrate)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) tenant synchronized with an on-premises Active Directory domain.  
  
Your company has an internally developed line-of-business (LOB) application.  
  
You need to implement SAML single sign-on (SSO) and require multi-factor authentication (MFA) when users try to access the application from an unknown location.  
  
Which two features should be included in the solution? Each correct answer represents part of the solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.
questions.explanation:
Azure AD enterprise applications provide the SAML SSO configuration for an application integrated with Azure AD. Conditional Access policies can target the application, evaluate network/location conditions, and require MFA for access outside trusted or named locations.

**Learn more:** [Enable SAML single sign-on for an enterprise application](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/enterprise-apps/add-application-portal-setup-sso) · [Require MFA for all users with Conditional Access](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/conditional-access/policy-all-users-mfa-strength)

questions.domain: Design identity, governance, and monitoring solutions
questions.question:
You must implement Azure RBAC role assignments for the Network Contributor role. The solution must satisfy the authentication and authorization requirements.  
  
What is the minimum number of assignments required?
questions.explanation: Azure RBAC role assignments at a management group scope automatically inherit to all subscriptions and resources below that scope. Since there are two separate Azure tenants, and each tenant has its own root management group hierarchy, one Network Contributor assignment per tenant root management group is required—a total of 2 assignments to cover both tenants and all their subscriptions.

questions.question:
You need to recommend a data-storage strategy for WebApp1.  
  
What should the recommendation include?

options.text: an Azure virtual machine that runs SQL Server
a fixed-size DTU Azure SQL database
an Azure SQL Database elastic pool

questions.explanation:
A vCore-based Azure SQL Database provides a PaaS database service and supports Azure Hybrid Benefit for SQL Server, allowing eligible existing SQL Server licenses to reduce database costs. The vCore model also provides independent selection of compute and storage resources.\
\
**Learn more:** [Purchasing models and service tiers - Azure SQL Database](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-sql/database/purchasing-models?view=azuresql)

questions.domain: Design identity, governance, and monitoring solutions
questions.question:
You need to recommend a data-storage strategy for WebApp1.  
  
What should the recommendation include?

options.text: one App Service Environment (ASE) per availability zone
one App Service Environment (ASE) per region
one App Service plan per region
one App Service plan per availability zone

questions.explanation:
An App Service plan is created in a region, and multiple apps in the same plan share the plan’s compute resources. App Service Environments provide dedicated isolation and require the Isolated v2 tier, making them more expensive than the multitenant App Service offering. Availability-zone resilience is configured by distributing plan instances across zones within a region, rather than by creating a plan for each zone.

**Learn more:** [Azure App Service plans](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/app-service/overview-hosting-plans) · [App Service Environment v3 and multitenant comparison](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/app-service/environment/ase-multi-tenant-comparison)

questions.question:
You have an Azure subscription containing 1,000 resources.  
  
You need to produce compliance reports for the subscription. The solution must allow the resources to be grouped by department.  
  
What should you use to organize the resources?
questions.explanation:
Azure Policy assesses resource compliance and provides compliance data and reporting for a subscription. Tags are key-value metadata that categorize resources by organizational attributes such as department, and Azure Policy can enforce consistent tag use at scale.\
\
**Learn more:** [Overview of Azure Policy](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/governance/policy/overview) · [Use tags to organize your Azure resources and management hierarchy](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-resource-manager/management/tag-resources)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have SQL Server running on an Azure virtual machine. The databases receive writes nightly as part of a batch process.  
  
You need to recommend a disaster recovery solution for the data. The solution must meet these requirements:  
  
- Provide the ability to recover from a regional outage.  
- Support a recovery time objective (RTO) of 15 minutes.  
- Support a recovery point objective (RPO) of 24 hours.  
- Support automated recovery.  
- Minimize costs.  
  
What should you include in the recommendation?
questions.explanation:
Azure Site Recovery replicates Azure virtual machines to a target region for regional disaster recovery and can orchestrate failover through recovery plans. For SQL Server workloads, Microsoft documents an expected Site Recovery RTO of typically less than 15 minutes; its asynchronous replication can meet a 24-hour RPO while avoiding the cost of a continuously active secondary SQL Server deployment.

**Learn more:** [Set up disaster recovery for SQL Server with Azure Site Recovery](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/site-recovery/site-recovery-sql) · [Reliability in Azure Site Recovery](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/reliability/reliability-site-recovery)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are developing a sales application that will include several Azure cloud services and handle different parts of a transaction. Different cloud services will process customer orders, billing, payment, inventory, and shipping.  
  
You need to recommend a solution that enables the cloud services to communicate transaction information asynchronously by using XML messages.  
  
What should you include in the recommendation?
questions.explanation:
Azure Service Bus is a fully managed enterprise message broker that decouples applications and services through queues and publish-subscribe topics. It supports asynchronous, store-and-forward communication, and its message payloads can carry structured data such as XML.

**Learn more:** [What is Azure Service Bus?](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-gb/azure/service-bus-messaging/service-bus-messaging-overview) · [Asynchronous messaging patterns and high availability](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/service-bus-messaging/service-bus-async-messaging)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You intend to deploy 10 applications to Azure. The applications will be deployed across two Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) clusters, with each cluster located in a separate Azure region.  
  
The application deployment must satisfy the following requirements:  
  
- Ensure that the applications stay available if one AKS cluster fails.  
- Ensure that internet connection traffic is encrypted by using SSL, without needing to configure SSL on every container.  
  
Which service should be included in the recommendation?
questions.explanation:
Azure Front Door is a global Layer 7 load balancer that monitors origin health and can fail over traffic from an unavailable AKS cluster to an alternate regional cluster. It also supports TLS/SSL termination (SSL offload) at the edge, avoiding SSL configuration on each application container.

**Learn more:** [Accelerate and secure your web application with Azure Front Door](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/frontdoor/scenarios) · [Azure Front Door best practices](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/frontdoor/best-practices)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription containing a Basic Azure virtual WAN named VirtualWAN1 and the virtual hubs shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783706725971-2qots6h6.png)  
  
You have an ExpressRoute circuit in the US East Azure region.  
  
You need to create an ExpressRoute association with VirtualWAN1.  
  
What should you do first?

options.text: Create a hub virtual network in US East.

questions.explanation:
A Basic Azure virtual WAN supports only site-to-site VPN. Upgrading it to Standard upgrades its hubs to Standard hubs, which support ExpressRoute and allow deployment of an ExpressRoute gateway for the circuit association. An ExpressRoute premium add-on is not inherently required, and the existing US East hub is the appropriate regional hub.

**Learn more:** [Azure Virtual WAN overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-wan/virtual-wan-about) · [Upgrade a virtual WAN from Basic to Standard](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-wan/upgrade-virtual-wan)

questions.domain: Design identity, governance, and monitoring solutions
questions.question:
You are planning a large Azure environment that will include many subscriptions.  
  
You intend to use Azure Policy as part of a governance solution.  
  
To which three scopes can Azure Policy definitions be assigned? Each correct answer provides a complete solution.  
  
**NOTE:** Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) administrative units

questions.explanation:
Azure Policy assignments can be applied at management group, subscription, and resource group scopes, with inheritance to contained resources. Management groups are particularly suited to governing multiple subscriptions consistently.\
\
**Learn more:** [Overview of Azure Policy](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/governance/policy/overview)

questions.domain: Design identity, governance, and monitoring solutions
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Entra ID Governance provides access reviews for applications. Designated reviewers, such as project managers, can periodically review application assignments and recertify or deny users’ continued access; review outcomes can automatically remove users who no longer require access. Recurring reviews can be scheduled every 30 days.

**Learn more:** [Plan a Microsoft Entra access reviews deployment](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/id-governance/deploy-access-reviews) · [Manage user and guest user access with access reviews](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/id-governance/manage-access-review)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You intend to deploy an app that will use an Azure Storage account.  
  
You must deploy the storage account. It must meet these requirements:  
  
- Store data for multiple users.  
- Encrypt each user's data with a separate key.  
- Encrypt all data in the storage account by using customer-managed keys.  
  
What should you deploy?

options.text: files in a premium file share storage account
blobs in a general purpose v2 storage account
blobs in an Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2 account
files in a general purpose v2 storage account

questions.explanation:
Blob Storage encryption scopes create separate encryption boundaries for data belonging to different customers or users. Each scope can use a customer-managed key from Azure Key Vault or Managed HSM and can be applied to a container or individual blob. A general-purpose v2 storage account supports Blob Storage and customer-managed keys for account encryption.

**Learn more:** [Encryption scopes for Blob storage - Azure Storage](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/blobs/encryption-scope-overview) · [Azure Storage encryption for data at rest](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/common/storage-service-encryption)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You need to recommend an Azure Storage solution that meets these requirements:  
  
- The storage must support 1 PB of data.  
- Data must be stored in blob storage.  
- The storage must support three levels of subfolders.  
- The storage must support access control lists (ACLs).  
  
What should you include in the recommendation?

options.text: a premium storage account that is configured for block blobs
a general purpose v2 storage account that has hierarchical namespace enabled
a premium storage account that is configured for page blobs
a premium storage account that is configured for file shares and supports large file shares

questions.explanation:
A general-purpose v2 storage account with hierarchical namespace enabled provides Azure Data Lake Storage capabilities: real nested directories and POSIX-compliant ACLs for blob data. Hierarchical namespace support preserves object-storage scalability, so it meets the 1 PB requirement.

**Learn more:** [Azure Data Lake Storage hierarchical namespace](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/blobs/data-lake-storage-namespace) · [Use the Azure portal to manage ACLs in Azure Data Lake Storage](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/blobs/data-lake-storage-acl-azure-portal)

questions.question:
You must recommend a solution for generating a monthly report of every new Azure Resource Manager (ARM) resource deployment in your Azure subscription.  
  
What should the recommendation include?
questions.explanation:
Azure Activity Log captures subscription-level Azure Resource Manager control-plane operations, including resource creation and deployment-related events. Its administrative events can be reviewed or filtered to identify new resource deployments over a monthly reporting period.\
\
**Learn more:** [Activity log in Azure Monitor](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/platform/activity-log) · [Azure Activity Log event schema](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/platform/activity-log-schema)

questions.question:
You have an on-premises storage solution.  
  
You need to migrate the solution to Azure. The solution must support the Hadoop Distributed File System (HDFS).  
  
What should you use?
questions.explanation:
Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2 provides a hierarchical namespace and Hadoop-compatible file-system access, enabling data to be managed through HDFS-compatible interfaces and the ABFS driver.\
\
**Learn more:** [Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2 overview in HDInsight](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/hdinsight/overview-data-lake-storage-gen2) · [Using the HDFS CLI with Azure Data Lake Storage](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/blobs/data-lake-storage-use-hdfs-data-lake-storage)

questions.question:
You have an on-premises storage solution.  
  
You need to migrate the solution to Azure. The solution must support the Hadoop Distributed File System (HDFS).  
  
What should you use?
questions.explanation:
KEDA provides event-driven autoscaling for Azure Functions containers on Kubernetes and supports Azure Storage Queue triggers. It feeds external event metrics to the Kubernetes Horizontal Pod Autoscaler (HPA), which scales the function pods. This preserves the Consumption-plan-style, queue-driven scaling model and does not depend on virtual nodes, which are unsupported with kubenet.

**Learn more:** [Azure Functions on Kubernetes with KEDA](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-functions/functions-kubernetes-keda) · [Kubernetes Event-driven Autoscaling (KEDA) on AKS](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/aks/keda-about)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You must design a highly available Azure SQL database that satisfies these requirements:  
  
- Failover between database replicas must take place without data loss.  
- The database must stay available if a zone outage occurs.  
- Costs must be kept to a minimum.  
  
Which deployment option should you use?

options.text: Azure SQL Managed Instance Business Critical
Azure SQL Managed Instance General Purpose

questions.explanation:
Azure SQL Database Premium supports zone redundancy, which distributes synchronous replicas across availability zones. This provides resilience to an availability-zone outage with no expected loss of committed data. The Basic tier does not support zone redundancy, and Azure SQL Managed Instance Business Critical is a more costly option for these requirements.

**Learn more:** [Reliability in Azure SQL Database](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/reliability/reliability-sql-database) · [Enable zone redundancy for Azure SQL Database](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-sql/database/enable-zone-redundancy?view=azuresql)

questions.question:
Web access-log data is stored in Azure Blob Storage.  
  
You plan to create monthly reports from the access logs.  
  
You need to recommend an automated process that uploads the data to Azure SQL Database each month.  
  
What should the recommendation include?
questions.explanation:
Azure Data Factory can orchestrate a scheduled monthly pipeline and use a Copy activity to load data from Azure Blob Storage into Azure SQL Database. Microsoft Learn documents this Blob Storage-to-Azure SQL Database pipeline pattern.\
\
**Learn more:** [Copy data from Azure Blob to Azure SQL Database using Azure Data Factory](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/data-factory/tutorial-copy-data-dot-net)

questions.question:
You need to recommend a solution that generates a monthly report of all new Azure Resource Manager (ARM) resource deployments in your Azure subscription.  
  
What should the recommendation include?
questions.explanation:
Azure activity logs capture Azure Resource Manager control-plane operations, including resource creation and deployment-related events. Sending the activity log to a Log Analytics workspace allows the events to be queried with KQL for a monthly report.\
\
**Learn more:** [Azure Monitor activity log](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/platform/activity-log) · [Monitor Azure Resource Manager](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-resource-manager/management/monitor-resource-manager)

questions.question:
You need to recommend a solution that generates a monthly report of all new Azure Resource Manager (ARM) resource deployments in your Azure subscription.  
  
What should the recommendation include?

options.text: Create an access policy for the blob service.
Modify the access level of the blob service.

questions.explanation:
An Azure Blob Storage container access policy can be used to configure a time-based immutability retention policy. Immutable storage provides write-once, read-many (WORM) protection: new blobs can be created and read, while protected existing data cannot be modified or deleted for the retention period. Azure Resource Manager locks do not protect blob contents from overwrite or deletion.

**Learn more:** [Configure immutability policies for containers - Azure Storage](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/blobs/immutable-policy-configure-container-scope) · [Overview of immutable storage for blob data - Azure Storage](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/blobs/immutable-storage-overview)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company operates offices in North America and Europe.  
  
You plan to migrate to Azure.  
  
You need to recommend a networking solution for the new Azure infrastructure. The solution must meet these requirements:  
  
- Point-to-Site (P2S) VPN connections for mobile users must automatically connect to the nearest Azure region.  
- Offices in each region must connect to their local Azure region by using an ExpressRoute circuit.  
- Transitive routing between virtual networks and on-premises networks must be supported.  
- Network traffic between virtual networks must be filtered by using FQDNs.  
  
What should you include in the recommendation?

options.text: Azure Virtual WAN with a secured virtual hub
virtual network peering and application security groups
virtual network gateways and network security groups (NSGs)
Azure Route Server and Azure Network Function Manager

questions.explanation:
Azure Virtual WAN provides regional virtual hubs with P2S and ExpressRoute gateway connectivity and managed transitive routing among connected virtual networks and on-premises networks. Its global User VPN profile directs a user to the closest Virtual WAN hub. A secured virtual hub integrates Azure Firewall for traffic inspection between virtual networks; Azure Firewall application rules support FQDN-based filtering.

**Learn more:** [Download global and hub VPN profiles for User VPN clients](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-wan/global-hub-profile) · [Azure Virtual WAN overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-wan/virtual-wan-about)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure virtual machine named VM1 that runs Windows Server 2019 and stores 500 GB of data files.  
  
You are designing a solution that will use Azure Data Factory to transform the data files and then load them into Azure Data Lake Storage.  
  
What should you deploy on VM1 to support this design?
questions.explanation:
A self-hosted integration runtime provides Azure Data Factory with compute and connectivity for data stores in a private network, including an Azure IaaS virtual machine. Installing it on VM1 lets Data Factory access and process the files before loading them to Azure Data Lake Storage.

**Learn more:** [Integration runtime in Azure Data Factory](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/data-factory/concepts-integration-runtime) · [Create and configure a self-hosted integration runtime](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/data-factory/create-self-hosted-integration-runtime)

questions.question:
You must recommend a storage solution for the records of a mission-critical application. The solution must provide a Service Level Agreement (SLA) for write-operation latency and throughput.  
  
What should you include in the recommendation?
questions.explanation:
Azure Cosmos DB provides SLA-backed write latency and guaranteed provisioned throughput, making it suitable for mission-critical workloads that require predictable performance. Its SLAs cover latency, throughput, consistency, and availability.\
\
**Learn more:** [Reliability in Azure Cosmos DB](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/reliability/reliability-cosmos-db) · [Optimize provisioned throughput cost in Azure Cosmos DB](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cosmos-db/optimize-cost-throughput)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have the resources shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783709421550-kgxixp0f.png)  
  
CDB1 contains a container that stores operational data updated continuously.  
  
You are designing a solution that uses AS1 to analyze the operational data each day.  
  
You need to recommend a solution that analyzes the data without affecting the performance of the operational data store.  
  
What should you include in the recommendation?

options.text: Azure Data Factory with Azure Cosmos DB and Azure Synapse Analytics connectors
Azure Synapse Analytics with PolyBase data loading
Azure Synapse Link for Azure Cosmos DB

questions.explanation:
Azure Synapse Link for Azure Cosmos DB enables Azure Synapse Analytics to query the Cosmos DB analytical store, which is a separately maintained, isolated column store. This supports analytics over continuously updated operational data without consuming the transactional workload’s provisioned throughput or affecting its performance.

**Learn more:** [What is Azure Synapse Link for Azure Cosmos DB?](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cosmos-db/synapse-link) · [What is Azure Cosmos DB analytical store?](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cosmos-db/analytical-store-introduction)

You intend to deploy Azure Cosmos DB databases that use the SQL API.  
  
You need to recommend a solution that gives specified Azure AD user accounts read access to the Cosmos DB databases.  
  
What should the recommendation include?

options.text: shared access signatures (SAS) and Conditional Access policies
master keys and Azure Information Protection policies
a resource token and an Access control (IAM) role assignment

questions.explanation:
Azure Cosmos DB SQL API resource tokens are generated from permission resources and can be restricted to read-only access for a specific resource and time period. An Access control (IAM) role assignment is used to assign Azure resource-management permissions to specified Microsoft Entra ID principals. This combination supports scoped Cosmos DB access for selected directory users.

- Failover between database replicas must occur with no data loss.  
- The database must stay available during an availability-zone outage.  
- Costs must be minimized.  
  
Which deployment option should you choose?

options.text: Azure SQL Managed Instance Business Critical
Azure SQL Managed Instance General Purpose

questions.explanation:
Azure SQL Database Business Critical uses synchronously replicated high-availability replicas. When configured for zone redundancy, replicas are distributed across availability zones, providing zero loss of committed data on failover and resilience to a single-zone outage. It meets these requirements without the additional managed-instance deployment cost.

You need to enable customer-managed Transparent Data Encryption (TDE) for the instance. The solution must maximize encryption strength.  
  
Which encryption-algorithm type and key length should you use for the TDE protector?
questions.explanation:
For Azure SQL Managed Instance customer-managed TDE, the protector must be an asymmetric RSA or RSA-HSM key. The supported RSA key lengths are 2,048 and 3,072 bits, so RSA 3072 provides the strongest supported option. AES 256 is symmetric and cannot serve as the TDE protector; RSA 4096 is unsupported.\
\
**Learn more:** [Azure SQL transparent data encryption with customer-managed key](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-sql/database/transparent-data-encryption-byok-overview?view=azuresql)

A Toronto branch office contains a virtual machine named VM1 that is configured as a file server. Users in all offices access the shared files on VM1.  
  
You need to recommend a solution that ensures users can access the shared files as quickly as possible if the Toronto branch office becomes inaccessible.  
  
What should you include in the recommendation?

questions.explanation:
Azure File Sync synchronizes Windows Server data with an Azure file share, which is the cloud endpoint for the sync group. The Azure file share provides an available cloud copy of the shared data when the Toronto file server cannot be reached, while Azure File Sync can also provide synchronized local server endpoints for branch-office access.

You must recommend a data storage solution that satisfies these requirements:  
  
- Ensures applications can access the data through a REST connection  
- Hosts 20 independent tables with different sizes and usage patterns  
- Automatically replicates data to a second Azure region  
- Minimizes costs  
  
What should you recommend?

options.text: an Azure SQL Database elastic pool that uses active geo-replication
tables in an Azure Storage account that use geo-redundant storage (GRS)
tables in an Azure Storage account that use read-access geo-redundant storage (RA-GRS)
an Azure SQL database that uses active geo-replication

questions.explanation:
Azure Table Storage provides a REST API for table data and supports geo-redundant storage (GRS), which asynchronously replicates the storage account’s data to a secondary Azure region. GRS meets the replication requirement at lower cost than RA-GRS because it does not add read access to the secondary region.

**Learn more:** [Table Storage REST API](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/rest/api/storageservices/table-service-rest-api) · [Data redundancy - Azure Storage](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/common/storage-redundancy)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are developing a sales application that will include several Azure cloud services and manage distinct parts of a transaction. Different cloud services will process customer orders, billing, payment, inventory, and shipping.  
  
You need to recommend a solution that lets the cloud services asynchronously exchange transaction information by using XML messages.  
  
What should you include in the recommendation?
questions.explanation:

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You need to design a highly available Azure SQL database that fulfills these requirements:  
  
- Failover between database replicas must take place with no data loss.  
- The database must stay available if a zone outage occurs.  
- Costs must be kept to a minimum.  
  
Which deployment option should be used?

questions.explanation:
The Business Critical tier provides several synchronous high-availability replicas. When zone redundancy is enabled, those replicas are distributed across availability zones, so a surviving replica can become primary after a zone failure with zero loss of committed data. Because Business Critical already includes the replicas used for this configuration, enabling zone redundancy does not add a separate charge, unlike zone-redundant Managed Instance General Purpose. lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You must design a highly available Azure SQL database that satisfies these requirements:

You are developing a sales application that will include several Azure cloud services and handle different components of a transaction. Different cloud services will process customer orders, billing, payment, inventory, and shipping.  
  
You need to recommend a solution that enables the cloud services to communicate transaction information asynchronously by using XML messages.  
  
What should you include in the recommendation?
questions.explanation:
Azure Queue Storage provides reliable, asynchronous message queues for communication between loosely coupled components of distributed applications. Services can enqueue transaction messages for other services to retrieve and process later; queue messages are UTF-8 text compatible with XML requests.

**Learn more:** [Tutorial: Work with Azure Queue Storage queues in .NET](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/queues/storage-tutorial-queues) · [Reliability in Azure Queue Storage](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/reliability/reliability-storage-queue)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You must design a highly available Azure SQL database that meets these requirements:  
  
- Failover between database replicas must take place with no data loss.  
- The database must stay available if an availability zone experiences an outage.  
- Costs must be kept to a minimum.  
  
Which deployment option should you use?

options.text: Azure SQL Managed Instance General Purpose

questions.explanation:
A zone-redundant Azure SQL Database Premium deployment places synchronous replicas in different availability zones. A transaction is committed only after it is persisted on sufficient secondary replicas, so a fully synchronized replica is available for failover with no loss of committed data. Premium also supports zone redundancy without an additional zone-redundancy charge because it uses its existing replicas.

**Learn more:** [Reliability in Azure SQL Database](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/reliability/reliability-sql-database)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You must design a highly available Azure SQL database that satisfies these requirements:

- Reads and writes temporary files on the local file system.  
- Writes to the Application event log.  
  
You need to recommend an Azure hosting solution for Service1. The solution must meet these requirements:  
  
- Minimize maintenance overhead.  
- Minimize costs.  
  
What should you include in the recommendation?

options.text: an Azure App Service web app
an Azure virtual machine scale set

questions.explanation:
Windows Azure virtual machine scale set instances provide local temporary disks and can use Windows Application event logs. Azure App Service blocks application code from accessing common Windows event logs, including the Application log; this limitation also rules out an App Service Environment and Azure Functions app. A VM scale set can automate instance management and scaling while meeting the required operating-system capabilities.

**Learn more:** [Operating System Functionality in Azure App Service](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-ca/azure/app-service/operating-system-functionality) · [FAQ for Azure Virtual Machine Scale Sets](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-machine-scale-sets/virtual-machine-scale-sets-faq)

You need to recommend a service to host the databases. The solution must meet these requirements:  
  
- Whenever possible, minimize management overhead for the migrated databases.  
- Ensure users can authenticate by using Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) credentials.  
- Minimize the number of database changes needed to facilitate the migration.  
  
What should you include in the recommendation?

questions.explanation:

You plan to deploy an Azure Database for MySQL flexible server named Server1 in the East US Azure region.  
  
You need to implement a business-continuity solution for Server1. The solution must minimize downtime if a failover to a paired region occurs.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Store the database files in Azure premium file shares.

questions.explanation:
A cross-region read replica provides a pre-created copy of the server that can be promoted to an independent read-write server and receive redirected application traffic during a regional failure. This avoids the variable recovery time required to create and restore a new server from geo-redundant backups. Microsoft documents read replicas as a disaster-recovery option and describes geo-redundant backup recovery as deploying a new server with variable RTO.

**Learn more:** [Overview of business continuity with Azure Database for MySQL - Flexible Server](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/mysql/flexible-server/concepts-business-continuity) · [Backup and restore in Azure Database for MySQL](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/mysql/flexible-server/concepts-backup-restore)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are designing a microservices architecture to support a web application.  
  
The solution must satisfy the following requirements:  
  
- Deploy the solution both on-premises and in Azure.  
- Support low-latency and hyper-scale operations.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783708073129-oaflmmou.png)  
  
- Permit independent upgrades for every microservice.  
- Define policies that perform automatic microservice repairs.  
  
You need to recommend a technology. What should you recommend?
questions.explanation:
Azure Service Fabric is a distributed-systems platform for scalable, reliable microservices that can run both in Azure and in standalone on-premises clusters. It supports services being independently versioned, deployed, upgraded, and scaled, and it provides health monitoring plus detection and restart of failed services. Its stateful services are intended for high-throughput, low-latency workloads at large scale.

**Learn more:** [Overview of Azure Service Fabric](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/service-fabric/service-fabric-overview) · [Introduction to microservices on Azure](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/service-fabric/service-fabric-overview-microservices)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription containing an Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) instance named AKS1. AKS1 hosts microservice-based APIs configured to listen on nondefault HTTP ports.  
  
You plan to deploy a Standard-tier Azure API Management instance named APIM1 to make the APIs available to external users.  
  
You need to ensure that the AKS1 APIs can be accessed by APIM1. The solution must meet these requirements:  
  
- Implement mTLS authentication between APIM1 and AKS1.  
- Minimize development effort.  
- Minimize costs.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Implement an external load balancer on AKS1.
Redeploy APIM1 to the virtual network that contains AKS1.
Implement an ExternalName service on AKS1.
Deploy an ingress controller to AKS1.

questions.explanation:
An ingress controller supplies a centralized Layer-7 entry point for HTTP APIs, routes requests to Kubernetes services on their configured ports, and can enforce mTLS at the cluster edge. Azure API Management natively supports mTLS, and Microsoft’s AKS/API Management guidance states that Kubernetes can enable this pattern by installing an ingress controller. This centralizes authentication and routing instead of requiring every microservice to implement them or exposing separate load balancers.

**Learn more:** [Use Azure API Management with microservices deployed in Azure Kubernetes Service](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/api-management/api-management-kubernetes) · [Best practices for network resources in Azure Kubernetes Service](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/aks/operator-best-practices-network)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You must design a highly available Azure SQL database that fulfills these requirements:  
  
- Failover between database replicas must take place with no data loss.  
- The database must stay available if an availability zone fails.  
- Costs must be kept to a minimum.  
  
Which deployment option should you use?

options.text: Azure SQL Managed Instance General Purpose

questions.explanation:
A zone-redundant Azure SQL Database Premium deployment distributes fully synchronized replicas across availability zones. A synchronized replica can become primary during a zone failure without loss of committed data. Premium supports zone redundancy, whereas the Standard tier does not; Premium also has no additional charge for enabling zone redundancy because it already uses multiple database replicas.

**Learn more:** [Reliability in Azure SQL Database](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/reliability/reliability-sql-database) · [Availability through local and zone redundancy for Azure SQL Database](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-sql/database/high-availability-sla-local-zone-redundancy)

questions.explanation:

You need to implement a storage solution for these files that meets the following requirements:  
  
- The files must be available within 24 hours after they are requested.  
- Storage costs must be minimized.  
  
Which two possible storage solutions meet this goal? Each correct answer provides a complete solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: Create an Azure Blob Storage account that is configured for the Cool default access tier. Create a blob container, copy the files to the blob container, and set each file to the Archive access tier.
Create a general-purpose v1 storage account. Create a blob container and copy the files to the blob container.
Create a general-purpose v2 storage account that is configured for the Cool default access tier. Create a file share in the storage account and copy the files to the file share.

Create a general-purpose v2 storage account that is configured for the Hot default access tier. Create a blob container, copy the files to the blob container, and set each file to the Archive access tier.

questions.explanation:
The Archive access tier is the lowest-cost tier for blob data that is rarely accessed. An archived blob can be rehydrated to an online tier in up to 15 hours, which meets a 24-hour availability requirement. Apache Spark directly reads the Azure Cosmos DB analytical store for near-real-time analysis, performs transformations and aggregations in Spark, and loads the resulting data into a dedicated SQL pool data warehouse. You have an on-premises Microsoft SQL Server 2008 instance that hosts a 50-GB database.  
  
You need to migrate the database to an Azure SQL Managed Instance. The solution must minimize downtime.  
  
What should you use?
questions.explanation:
Azure Data Studio supports the Azure SQL migration workflow for moving SQL Server databases to Azure SQL Managed Instance. Its online migration capability uses continuous data synchronization during migration, so downtime is limited to the final cutover rather than the full transfer of the 50-GB database.\
\
**Learn more:** [Migration overview: SQL Server to Azure SQL Managed Instance](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/data-migration/sql-server/managed-instance/overview)

You plan to migrate DB1 and DB2 to Azure.  
  
You need to recommend an Azure solution to host DB1 and DB2. The solution must meet these requirements:  
  
- Support server-side transactions across DB1 and DB2.  
- Minimize the administrative effort required to update the solution.  
  
What should you recommend?

options.text: two Azure SQL databases in an elastic pool
two databases on the same Azure SQL managed instance
two databases on the same SQL Server instance on an Azure virtual machine
two Azure SQL databases on different Azure SQL Database servers

questions.explanation:
Azure SQL Managed Instance supports server-side distributed transactions written in Transact-SQL across databases. As a managed PaaS service, it also reduces operating-system and SQL Server update administration compared with SQL Server hosted on an Azure virtual machine.

**Learn more:** [Distributed transactions across cloud databases](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-sql/database/elastic-transactions-overview?view=azuresql) · [Distributed Transaction Coordinator (DTC) for Azure SQL Managed Instance](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-sql/managed-instance/distributed-transaction-coordinator-dtc?view=azuresql)

Solution: An Azure virtual machine scale set that uses autoscaling is deployed.  
  
Does this satisfy the goal?
questions.explanation:
Autoscaling a Virtual Machine Scale Set adjusts instance capacity within its deployment region; it does not create a second regional deployment or configure cross-region failover. Therefore, the solution does not provide redundancy when an Azure region fails, even though virtual machines allow operating-system administration and can run the full .NET Framework.\
\
**Learn more:** [Reliability in Azure Virtual Machine Scale Sets](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/reliability/reliability-virtual-machine-scale-sets) · [Azure Virtual Machine Scale Sets overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-machine-scale-sets/overview)

questions.question:
Solution: You deploy two Azure virtual machines across two Azure regions and deploy an Azure Application Gateway.  
  
Does this satisfy the goal?
questions.explanation:
Azure Application Gateway v2 is a single-region service and becomes unavailable if its region fails. Multi-region resilience requires separate gateways in the target regions and a global load-balancing service, such as Azure Traffic Manager or Azure Front Door, to route and fail over traffic between them.\
\
**Learn more:** [Reliability in Azure Application Gateway v2](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/reliability/reliability-application-gateway-v2)

questions.domain: Design identity, governance, and monitoring solutions
questions.question:
Solution: Deploy two Azure virtual machines in two Azure regions and create an Azure Traffic Manager profile.  
  
Does this satisfy the goal?
questions.explanation:
Azure virtual machines provide control of the guest operating system and can host applications that require the full .NET Framework. With one VM in each of two regions, Azure Traffic Manager can monitor the endpoints and route traffic to the healthy regional instance during a regional outage, providing the required regional redundancy.\
\
**Learn more:** [Azure Traffic Manager FAQ](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/traffic-manager/traffic-manager-faqs) · [Quickstart: Create a Traffic Manager profile using the Azure portal](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/traffic-manager/quickstart-create-traffic-manager-profile)

questions.question:
Solution: You deploy a web app by using an Isolated App Service plan.  
  
Does this satisfy the goal?
questions.explanation:
An Isolated App Service plan is still a managed Azure App Service platform, rather than administrator-controlled operating-system infrastructure. It therefore does not provide administrators with OS access to install custom application dependencies, and a single regional deployment does not provide redundancy against an Azure region failure. A multi-region design on infrastructure with the required operating-system control is needed.\
\
**Learn more:** [What are Azure App Service plans?](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/app-service/overview-hosting-plans) · [Reliability in Azure App Service Environment](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/reliability/reliability-app-service-environment)

Azure SQL Managed Instance General Purpose

questions.explanation:
Azure SQL Database Premium supports zone redundancy, distributing synchronous database replicas across availability zones. Synchronous replication preserves committed data during failover, and zone redundancy keeps the database resilient to an availability-zone outage. Azure SQL Database Standard does not support zone redundancy, while a Business Critical managed instance provides capabilities beyond those required at a higher cost.

**Learn more:** [Reliability in Azure SQL Database](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/reliability/reliability-sql-database)

Does this meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
An Azure Policy initiative can include the built-in **Allowed locations** policy and assign the permitted region values. That policy uses a deny effect to prevent deployment of resources outside the approved locations, enforcing geo-compliance requirements for the App Service instances.\
\
**Learn more:** [Azure Policy overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/governance/policy/overview) · [Tutorial: Create and manage policies to enforce compliance](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/governance/policy/tutorials/create-and-manage)

questions.question:
Solution: You recommend creating resource groups based on location and applying resource locks to those resource groups.  
  
Does this meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
Azure resource locks protect resources from deletion or modification; they do not limit the Azure regions in which resources can be created. Enforcing deployment only to approved regions requires an Azure Policy assignment that restricts allowed locations.\
\
**Learn more:** [Lock your Azure resources to protect your infrastructure](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-resource-manager/management/lock-resources) · [Tutorial: Disallow resource types in your cloud environment](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/governance/policy/tutorials/disallowed-resources)

questions.question:
Solution: You recommend using the Regulatory compliance dashboard in Microsoft Defender for Cloud.  
  
Does this satisfy the goal?
questions.explanation:
The Regulatory compliance dashboard continuously assesses resources against compliance controls and reports their compliance state, but it does not prevent deployments outside specified regions. Azure Policy can enforce that Azure resources are deployed only to allowed regions.\
\
**Learn more:** [Regulatory compliance standards in Microsoft Defender for Cloud](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-ie/azure/defender-for-cloud/concept-regulatory-compliance-standards) · [What is Azure Policy?](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/governance/policy/overview)

questions.question:
Solution: You recommend using an Azure Policy initiative that enforces the location of resource groups.  
  
Does this meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
Resource-group location enforcement does not control the deployment locations of the resources contained in those groups. Azure Policy must evaluate and restrict the locations of the App Service resources themselves to enforce approved regions and regional co-location. Microsoft documents that policies enforcing location on resource groups specifically target the `Microsoft.Resources/subscriptions/resourceGroups` resource type, while the built-in **Allowed locations** policy restricts locations for new resources.\
\
**Learn more:** [Azure Policy definition structure basics](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/governance/policy/concepts/definition-structure-basics) · [Azure Policy overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/governance/policy/overview)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You must design a highly available Azure SQL database that satisfies these requirements:  
  
- Failover between database replicas must take place with no data loss.  
- The database must stay available if a zone outage occurs.  
- Costs must be kept to a minimum.  
  
Which deployment option should you use?

options.text: Azure SQL Managed Instance General Purpose
Azure SQL Managed Instance Business Critical

questions.explanation:
Azure SQL Database Premium can be configured for zone redundancy, placing replicas in separate availability zones. Its primary replica persists changes to synchronized secondary replicas before committing transactions, ensuring a fully synchronized replica is available for failover; Azure documents no expected data loss during a zone failover. Premium already provides multiple replicas, so distributing them across zones incurs no additional zone-redundancy charge.

**Learn more:** [Reliability in Azure SQL Database](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/reliability/reliability-sql-database)

questions.question: What should be recommended to fulfill the monitoring requirements for App2?
questions.explanation: Azure Application Insights is an Application Performance Management (APM) service that monitors application-level metrics including transaction performance, response times, and event durations across end-to-end flows. This directly supports analysis of application behavior and transaction diagnostics. VM Insights (A) applies to virtual machines, Microsoft Sentinel (C) is a SIEM, and Container Insights (D) monitors containerized workloads—none are appropriate for App Service monitoring.

questions.explanation:
Dynamic data masking limits exposure of sensitive columns by returning masked values to nonprivileged users while privileged users can be granted permission to view the unmasked data. Transparent Data Encryption protects data at rest, Data Discovery & Classification identifies and labels sensitive data, and Azure RBAC does not provide column-level masking of query results. All Azure resources must be readily identifiable by the following operational information: environment, owner, department, and cost center.

You have an on-premises line-of-business (LOB) application that uses a Microsoft SQL Server instance for its backend.  
  
You plan to migrate the on-premises SQL Server instance to Azure virtual machines.  
  
You need to recommend a highly available SQL Server deployment that meets these requirements:  
  
- Minimizes costs  
- Minimizes failover time if a single server fails  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783708094177-s6nxdupd.png)  
  
What should you include in the recommendation?

options.text: an Always On availability group that has premium storage disks and a virtual network name (VNN)
an Always On Failover Cluster Instance that has a virtual network name (VNN) and a standard file share
an Always On availability group that has premium storage disks and a distributed network name (DNN)
an Always On Failover Cluster Instance that has a virtual network name (VNN) and a premium file share

questions.explanation:
An Always On availability group with a distributed network name (DNN) listener avoids the Azure Load Balancer required by a virtual network name (VNN) listener in a single-subnet deployment. Removing that dependency lowers deployment and management overhead and avoids the load balancer’s health-probe delay, making failover faster. Availability groups protect at the database level without the shared storage required for a failover cluster instance. [Configure a DNN listener for an availability group](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-sql/virtual-machines/windows/availability-group-distributed-network-name-dnn-listener-configure?view=azuresql)

**Learn more:** [Configure a DNN listener for an availability group](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-sql/virtual-machines/windows/availability-group-distributed-network-name-dnn-listener-configure?view=azuresql) · [Always On availability groups on SQL Server on Azure VMs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-sql/virtual-machines/windows/availability-group-overview?view=azuresql-vm)

Solution: Use Azure Advisor for network-traffic analysis.  
  
Does this satisfy the goal?
questions.explanation:
Azure Advisor does not determine whether specific packets to or from virtual machines are allowed or denied. Azure Network Watcher IP flow verify performs that diagnostic by evaluating the configured security and admin rules and returning an allowed or denied result.\
\
**Learn more:** [IP flow verify overview — Azure Network Watcher](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/network-watcher/ip-flow-verify-overview)

questions.question:
Solution: Use Azure Traffic Analytics in Azure Network Watcher to analyze network traffic.  
  
Does this satisfy the goal?
questions.explanation:
Azure Traffic Analytics analyzes Azure Network Watcher flow logs and provides visibility into allowed and blocked traffic, including the rules that block flows. It can therefore identify whether traffic to Azure virtual machines is allowed or denied.\
\
**Learn more:** [Traffic Analytics Overview - Azure Network Watcher](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/network-watcher/traffic-analytics)

questions.question:
Solution: Use Azure Network Watcher to run IP flow verify for network-traffic analysis.  
  
Does this satisfy the goal?
questions.explanation:
Azure Network Watcher IP flow verify tests a specified TCP or UDP flow to or from an Azure virtual machine against the applicable security and admin rules. It returns whether access is allowed or denied and identifies the rule responsible, enabling diagnosis of virtual-machine traffic-filtering issues.\
\
**Learn more:** [IP Flow Verify Overview - Azure Network Watcher](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/network-watcher/ip-flow-verify-overview) · [Diagnose a virtual machine network traffic filter problem](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-network/diagnose-network-traffic-filter-problem)

questions.domain: Design identity, governance, and monitoring solutions
questions.question:
Solution: Install and configure the Azure Monitor Agent and the Dependency Agent on every virtual machine. Use VM insights in Azure Monitor to analyze network traffic.  
  
Does this satisfy the goal?
questions.explanation:
VM insights uses the Dependency Agent for process and connection-dependency data; it does not determine whether a packet is permitted or blocked by network security rules. Azure Network Watcher IP flow verify evaluates the applicable security and admin rules for a virtual machine and reports whether the specified traffic is allowed or denied.\
\
**Learn more:** [IP flow verify overview - Azure Network Watcher](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/network-watcher/ip-flow-verify-overview) · [Dependency Agent in Azure Monitor VM insights](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/vm/vminsights-dependency-agent)

You need to recommend a solution that lets the cloud services asynchronously exchange transaction information by using XML messages.  
  
What should you include in the recommendation?
questions.explanation:
Azure Queue Storage provides durable queues for asynchronous communication between distributed application components, allowing transaction-processing services to be decoupled. Queue messages must be compatible with UTF-8 XML requests, which meets the XML-message requirement.

Sub1 contains an Azure App Service web app named App1. App1 uses Azure AD for single-tenant user authentication. Users from contoso.com can authenticate to App1.  
  
You need to recommend a solution that enables users in the fabrikam.com tenant to authenticate to App1.  
  
What should you recommend?

options.text: Configure Supported account types in the application registration and update the sign-in endpoint.

questions.explanation:
A multitenant Microsoft Entra application allows organizational users from other tenants to sign in. Changing the app registration’s Supported account types to allow accounts in any organizational directory and using a multitenant sign-in authority endpoint enables fabrikam.com users to authenticate to the app.

**Learn more:** [Convert single-tenant app to multitenant on Microsoft Entra ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity-platform/howto-convert-app-to-be-multi-tenant) · [Identity and account types for single- and multitenant apps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/security/zero-trust/develop/identity-supported-account-types)

Enable Azure AD pass-through authentication and update the sign-in endpoint.
Configure assignments for the fabrikam.com users by using Azure AD Privileged Identity Management (PIM).

An access package can govern Fabrikam users' lifecycle and application access while they authenticate through their home tenant.

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You plan to migrate on-premises MySQL databases to Azure Database for MySQL Flexible Server.  
  
You need to recommend a configuration solution for Azure Database for MySQL Flexible Server. The solution must meet the following requirements:  
  
- The databases must remain accessible if a datacenter fails.  
- Costs must be minimized.  
  
Which compute tier should you recommend?
questions.explanation:
Zone-redundant high availability provides resilience to an availability-zone/datacenter failure by using a standby server in another zone. The Burstable tier does not support high availability. General Purpose supports production workloads and high availability without the additional memory-focused capacity and cost of the Memory Optimized tier.

**Learn more:** [High availability concepts in Azure Database for MySQL - Flexible Server](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/mysql/flexible-server/concepts-high-availability) · [Azure Database for MySQL - Flexible Server service tiers](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/mysql/flexible-server/concepts-service-tiers-storage)

questions.question:
You need to recommend a solution that produces a monthly report of all new Azure Resource Manager (ARM) resource deployments in your Azure subscription.  
  
What should the recommendation include?
questions.explanation:
Azure Activity Log records Azure Resource Manager control-plane deployment operations. Sending the activity log to a Log Analytics workspace stores the events in the `AzureActivity` table, where they can be queried and used to produce a monthly deployment report.\
\
**Learn more:** [Azure Monitor activity log](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/platform/activity-log)

You must recommend a solution that fulfills the database retention requirements.  
  
What should you recommend?

options.text: Configure a long-term retention policy for the database.
Use automatic Azure SQL Database backups.

questions.explanation:
An Azure SQL Database long-term retention (LTR) policy automatically retains database backups in separate Azure Blob storage for the configured weekly, monthly, and yearly periods, for up to 10 years. This directly satisfies long-term database-retention requirements.\
\
**Learn more:** [Manage Azure SQL Database long-term backup retention](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-sql/database/long-term-backup-retention-configure?view=azuresql)

questions.question:
You have an Azure subscription.  
  
You need to recommend an Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) solution that uses Linux nodes. The solution must meet the following requirements:  
  
- Minimize the time required to provision compute resources during scale-out operations.  
- Support autoscaling for Linux containers.  
- Minimize administrative effort.  
  
Which scaling option should you recommend?
questions.explanation:
AKS virtual nodes use Azure Container Instances to provision pods rapidly, without waiting for the cluster autoscaler to deploy VM compute nodes. They are supported for Linux pods and nodes, and the serverless container infrastructure reduces node-administration overhead.\
\
**Learn more:** [Use virtual nodes with Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/aks/virtual-nodes)

You have an Azure subscription that contains a blob container with multiple blobs.  
  
Ten users in your company's finance department plan to access the blobs during April.  
  
You need to recommend a solution that enables access to the blobs only for the month of April.  
  
Which security solution should be included in the recommendation?
questions.explanation:
A shared access signature (SAS) provides delegated, granular access to Azure Storage resources, including blob containers and blobs. Its permissions and validity interval can be set so access begins and expires during April only.\
\
**Learn more:** [Grant limited access to Azure Storage resources using shared access signatures (SAS)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/common/storage-sas-overview)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are designing an application that will be hosted in Azure.  
  
The application will store video files ranging from 50 MB to 12 GB. It will use certificate-based authentication and be available to users on the internet.  
  
You need to recommend a storage option for the video files. The solution must deliver the fastest read performance while minimizing storage costs.  
  
What should you recommend?
questions.explanation:
Azure Blob Storage is optimized for massive amounts of unstructured data and is designed for distributed file access and streaming video and audio over HTTP/HTTPS. Block blobs support access tiers, enabling storage costs to be optimized for the files’ access pattern while online tiers provide immediate retrieval.

**Learn more:** [Introduction to Azure Blob Storage](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/blobs/storage-blobs-introduction) · [Access tiers for blob data](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/blobs/access-tiers-overview)

questions.question:
You need to recommend a solution that generates a monthly report covering all new Azure Resource Manager (ARM) resource deployments in your Azure subscription.  
  
What should the recommendation include?
questions.explanation:
Azure Activity Log records Azure Resource Manager control-plane operations, including resource creation and deployment-related events. Routing that data to an Azure Log Analytics workspace allows it to be queried over a monthly period to produce a report of new deployments.\
\
**Learn more:** [Activity log in Azure Monitor](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/platform/activity-log) · [Monitor Azure Resource Manager](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-resource-manager/management/monitor-resource-manager)
